blocks.prompt:
5 (i) Solve the following matrix equation for \(X\): \(2X - 3A = B\) if
\[A = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 3 & -2 \\ -1 & 1 & 5\end{bmatrix}\]
and
\[B = \begin{bmatrix}2 & -3 & 1 \\ 5 & 4 & -1\end{bmatrix}\]
blocks.explanation:
Yeh matrix equation hai: is mein unknown \(X\) koi number nahi, poori matrix hai.
Diya kya hai? \(2X - 3A = B\), aur \(A\), \(B\) dono \(2 \times 3\).
Find kya karna hai? Matrix \(X\).
Rule kaunsa? Matrix addition aur scalar multiplication ke qawaid, jo bilkul algebra jaise chalte hain.
Plan: \(X\) ko akela karna: \(X = \frac{1}{2}(B + 3A)\); phir \(3A\), us mein \(B\) jama, aadha, aur aakhir mein di hui equation mein tasdeeq.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(2X - 3A = B\), jahan \(A\) aur \(B\) ka order \(2 \times 3\) hai.
Humein find karna hai: \(X\).
Tareeqa: Agar yeh numbers ki equation \(2x - 3a = b\) hoti to hum \(3a\) ko doosri taraf le ja kar 2 se divide karte. Matrices mein addition aur scalar (aam number) se multiplication bilkul isi tarah kaam karte hain, is liye wohi tareeqa lagayenge. Bas yaad rahe ke matrix se 'divide' nahi karte; hum scalar \(\frac{1}{2}\) se multiply karenge.

\(X\) ko akela karein
\[2X = B + 3A\]
\[X = \dfrac{1}{2}(B + 3A)\]
Kyun: Dono taraf \(3A\) jama kiya to left par sirf \(2X\) bacha. Phir dono taraf ko scalar \(\frac{1}{2}\) se multiply kiya. \(X\) ka order bhi \(B\) jitna, yani \(2 \times 3\), hoga, kyunke same order ki matrices hi jama ho sakti hain.
Dhyan dein: \(-3A\) doosri taraf ja kar \(+3A\) banta hai, \(-3A\) nahi.

\(3A\) nikalein
\[3A = \begin{bmatrix}6 & 9 & -6 \\ -3 & 3 & 15\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: Scalar multiplication mein matrix ki har entry ko 3 se zarb dete hain: \(3(2) = 6\), \(3(3) = 9\), \(3(-2) = -6\), \(3(-1) = -3\), \(3(1) = 3\), \(3(5) = 15\).

\(B\) jama karein
\[B + 3A = \begin{bmatrix}2 + 6 & -3 + 9 & 1 - 6 \\ 5 - 3 & 4 + 3 & -1 + 15\end{bmatrix}\]
\[= \begin{bmatrix}8 & 6 & -5 \\ 2 & 7 & 14\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: Same jagah wali entries jama hoti hain. Signs ka khayal: \(1 + (-6) = -5\) aur \(5 + (-3) = 2\).

\(\frac{1}{2}\) se multiply karein
\[X = \begin{bmatrix}4 & 3 & -\frac{5}{2} \\ 1 & \frac{7}{2} & 7\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: Har entry ko aadha kiya: \(8/2 = 4\), \(6/2 = 3\), \(-5/2 = -2.5\), \(2/2 = 1\), \(7/2 = 3.5\), \(14/2 = 7\). Fraction ya decimal dono tarah likh sakte hain; kitab ki answer key decimal mein likhti hai.

Tasdeeq: di hui equation mein rakhein
\[2X = \begin{bmatrix}8 & 6 & -5 \\ 2 & 7 & 14\end{bmatrix}\]
\[2X - 3A = \begin{bmatrix}2 & -3 & 1 \\ 5 & 4 & -1\end{bmatrix} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(2X\) mein se \(3A\) minus kiya: \(8 - 6 = 2\), \(6 - 9 = -3\), \(-5 - (-6) = 1\), \(2 - (-3) = 5\), \(7 - 3 = 4\), \(14 - 15 = -1\). Yeh bilkul \(B\) hai, is liye \(X\) sahi hai.

blocks.prompt:
5 (ii) Solve the following matrix equation for \(X\): \(A^2 - 5A + 4I - X = 0\) if
\[A = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{bmatrix}\]
blocks.explanation:
Yeh bhi matrix equation hai, lekin is mein \(A^2\) bhi hai.
Diya kya hai? \(A^2 - 5A + 4I - X = O\) aur \(3 \times 3\) matrix \(A\).
Find kya karna hai? \(X\).
Rule kaunsa? \(X\) ko akela karna, phir matrix multiplication (\(A^2 = AA\)), scalar multiplication aur identity matrix.
Plan: \(X = A^2 - 5A + 4I\); \(A^2\) row by row, phir \(5A\) aur \(4I\), sab jor kar \(X\), aur factorise kar ke tasdeeq.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(A^2 - 5A + 4I - X = O\), jahan \(A\) ka order \(3 \times 3\) aur \(I = I_3\) hai.
Humein find karna hai: \(X\).
Tareeqa: Dono taraf \(X\) jama karne se \(X = A^2 - 5A + 4I\) mil jata hai. Phir teen hisse alag alag nikal kar jorenge. \(A^2\) ka matlab hai \(A\) ko \(A\) se multiply karna, har entry ka square nahi.

\(X\) ko akela karein
\[X = A^2 - 5A + 4I\]
Kyun: Equation ke left par \(-X\) hai aur right par zero matrix \(O\). Dono taraf \(X\) jama kiya to \(X\) right par aa gaya. Ab \(X\) ki value seedha hisaab se milegi.

\(A^2 = AA\) ki pehli row
\[(2)(2) + (0)(2) + (1)(1) = 5\]
\[(2)(0) + (0)(1) + (1)(-1) = -1\]
\[(2)(1) + (0)(3) + (1)(0) = 2\]
Kyun: \(A\) ki pehli row \((2, 0, 1)\) ko \(A\) ke teeno columns \((2, 2, 1)\), \((0, 1, -1)\), \((1, 3, 0)\) se baari baari multiply kiya.
Dhyan dein: \(A^2\) ki entries ko \(A\) ki entries ka square samajhna (jaise \(2^2 = 4\)) bohat aam ghalti hai; \(A^2\) ki pehli entry 4 nahi, 5 hai.

\(A^2\), \(5A\) aur \(4I\) likhein
\[A^2 = \begin{bmatrix}5 & -1 & 2 \\ 9 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & -1 & -2\end{bmatrix}\]
\[5A = \begin{bmatrix}10 & 0 & 5 \\ 10 & 5 & 15 \\ 5 & -5 & 0\end{bmatrix}\]
\[4I = \begin{bmatrix}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: \(5A\) mein \(A\) ki har entry ko 5 se zarb diya. \(4I\) mein identity matrix ki har entry 4 se zarb hui, is liye diagonal par 4 aur baaqi jagah 0. Yahan \(I\) ka order 3 hai taake teeno matrices ka order same ho aur jama ho saken.

Sab jor kar \(X\) nikalein
\[X = \begin{bmatrix}5 - 10 + 4 & -1 - 0 + 0 & 2 - 5 + 0 \\ 9 - 10 + 0 & -2 - 5 + 4 & 5 - 15 + 0 \\ 0 - 5 + 0 & -1 + 5 + 0 & -2 - 0 + 4\end{bmatrix}\]
\[X = \begin{bmatrix}-1 & -1 & -3 \\ -1 & -3 & -10 \\ -5 & 4 & 2\end{bmatrix}\]
Kyun: Har jagah: \(A^2\) ki entry minus \(5A\) ki entry plus \(4I\) ki entry. \(4I\) ka 4 sirf diagonal (1,1), (2,2), (3,3) par jurta hai; baaqi jagah 0 jurta hai.
Dhyan dein: \(4I\) ko 'har entry mein 4 jama' samajh lena aam ghalti hai; 4 sirf diagonal par jata hai.

Tasdeeq: factorise kar ke
\[X = (A - I)(A - 4I)\]
\[\text{Row 1: } (1, 0, 1)\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 0 & 1 \\ 2 & -3 & 3 \\ 1 & -1 & -4\end{bmatrix}\]
\[= (-1,\ -1,\ -3) \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(x^2 - 5x + 4 = (x - 1)(x - 4)\) hota hai. Matrices mein yeh tab chalta hai jab matrices commute karein, aur \(A\) aur \(I\) hamesha commute karti hain (\(AI = IA = A\)). \(A - I\) ki pehli row \((1, 0, 1)\) ko \(A - 4I\) se multiply kiya: \(-2 + 0 + 1 = -1\), \(0 + 0 - 1 = -1\), \(1 + 0 - 4 = -3\). Doosre raaste se bhi \(X\) ki pehli row wohi aayi.
